findings.summary: Criterion 3 case (c) does not state the expected parser result
findings.evidence: The case says output with only a '---- name stdout ----' block and no list "yields the `(did not finish)`-free empty or count-mismatch result as the parser rule defines". That names two different outcomes, so the test's assertion is left open. Under step 2's rule, a section that has a `test result: ... 1 failed` line but no names listed gets the `<binary> (did not finish)` marker; it does not give an empty list. Fix: Split it into two cases with exact expected values. A section with `test result: FAILED ... 1 failed` and no indented list gives [`<binary> (did not finish)`]. Output with no `Running`/`Doc-tests` header gives [].

findings.summary: The reading calls the whole cause 'the root cause', but the plan fixes only the different-test case; the change description must keep the clash case out of the claim
findings.evidence: The request names two cases: a failure already on the base, and a clash with a concurrent config and test change. The reading's Fix shape addresses only the per-test comparison. The plan says so honestly (Decision 8, Open questions). Criterion 1 asks for the root cause to be 'fixed where it originates'. A reviewer could read that as covering both cases. Fix: Keep the statement that only case (a) is covered in the change description (pull request body) as well as in CHANGELOG and the design note. Name the follow-up needed for case (b), a check against the moved base, as a proposed separate job.

findings.summary: The note that Athena added the flag is not run through the redactor and should stay a fixed string
findings.evidence: `note` is built from fixed strings or `deadline_note` (checks.rs:233-263). `timed_out` reads the note. The plan appends a fixed phrase only on failed runs, which is safe. Fix: Add the phrase as a constant and append it after any existing note, separated by '; ', as `mark_pre_existing` does. Then a deadline or zero-tests note stays first.

summary: The plan fixes the comparison where the fault starts. `is_pre_existing` (verify.rs:134) relies on `Baseline::failed_before`, which matches by check name only. The plan records failing test names on `CheckRun` from `run_check` (checks.rs:190), which produces both the baseline and the job's own runs, and compares per test, falling back to today's name-level rule when either side has no names. I checked the code. The plan's list of struct literals needing the new field is complete (routing.rs:214 builds from `..skipped_run`), which covers Athena's eight findings about files outside the deliverables. `CheckRun` rejects unknown fields (records.rs:749-760), so the serde default plus skip-when-empty keeps old records loading. Minor findings never block (verify.rs:504), so the new split finding does not count a failure twice. The configured test check is `cargo test --locked` (athena.toml:96), so `cargo_test_args` applies. No crate sets `harness = false`, so the did-not-finish marker will not fire falsely. The criterion 2 and 5 tests run real records through the real `is_pre_existing`, `mark_pre_existing` and `judge` functions, with no fakes, and would fail under the name-only rule. The approach is sound: it parses cargo's own failure list per binary, labels names by binary, and uses --no-fail-fast plus a per-binary completeness check so a crash or incomplete list blocks rather than being excused. The plan says plainly that it does not handle a clash with a concurrent change, which needs a rebase or merge check that is out of scope. That scoping is right. Remaining points are minor: one parser test case does not state its expected result, and the change description should repeat the narrower scope.
